1. A system for assessment of head impacts, comprising:
a head-mounted device capable of being worn on or secured to the head of an individual, wherein the device is further capable of measuring angular head motion when worn or secured to the head of an individual;
memory in communication with the device via an interface;
a processor that reads instructions stored in the memory, wherein the instructions direct the processor to:
obtain head kinematic measurements in at least one anatomical direction from the head-mounted device;
compute, utilizing the head kinematic measurements, a head kinematic metric for the at least one anatomical direction;
determine that a concussive event occurs utilizing a trained classifier and the head kinematic metric.
2. The system of claim 1, wherein the head mounted device is a helmet, a mouth guard, a hat, an ear protection, an eye-wear, a skin-mounted sensor, or a head band.
3. The system of claim 1 further comprising a gyroscope, a rotational accelerometer, or an array of linear accelerometers to measure head angular motion.
4. The system of claim 1, wherein the head kinematic metric is peak angular acceleration (a), peak change in rotational velocity (A), or peak translational acceleration (a).
5. The system of claim 1, wherein the head kinematic metric is a brain angle metric that is computed utilizing a mass-deformation brain model.
6. The system of claim 5, wherein the mass-deformation brain model is a mass- spring-damper model.
7. The system of claim 6, wherein the mass-spring-damper model models the rotational deformation of the brain from skull loading.

9. The system of claim 1, wherein the head kinematic measurements include head angle motion measurements in at least three anatomical directions.
10. The system of claim 9, wherein the three anatomical directions are coronal, axial, and sagittal.
